nate_dev: Hey team — after upgrading the SDK I'm getting a TypeError when starting my app. stack trace: 
```
TypeError: run_sync() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout'
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/transport/session.py", line 88, in request
    return self._client.run_sync(..., timeout=timeout)
```
I didn't change our code, just `pip install -U redwood-sdk` in CI. Any ideas? :thinking:

ana_support: Sorry you're hitting that. Can you share the output of `pip freeze` from the environment where it fails? Also, what's your Python version and OS?

nate_dev: Sure — running in Azure Linux container, Python 3.10. pip freeze: 
```
aiohttp==3.8.1
redwood-sdk==0.14.2
packaging==23.1
```
We pin aiohttp elsewhere in the monorepo constraints file to 3.8.1 (company-wide).

sam_engineer: Quick hypothesis: our new SDK release switched the internal sync adapter to rely on `aiohttp.ClientSession.run_sync` shim available in aiohttp >= 3.9 (we added a compatibility layer). If CI has 3.8.x the method signature or presence differs and that TypeError can occur.

nate_dev: Ah — that would line up. We never pinned redwood-sdk, just the global aiohttp constraint. Is the SDK supposed to work with 3.8?

sam_engineer: The SDK 0.14.x body changed to assume aiohttp>=3.9 when the `sync` helper was introduced. We should have documented it in the changelog better, sorry. Two short fixes: 
1) Loosen the monorepo constraint to allow aiohttp>=3.9, or 
2) Pin redwood-sdk to 0.13.x until you can lift aiohttp.

ana_support: For a quick repro, can you try in a local venv: `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install redwood-sdk==0.14.2 aiohttp==3.8.1` and confirm error? If yes, we'll scope as a compatibility bug and patch.

nate_dev: Reproduced locally following your steps — same TypeError. Confirmed.

sam_engineer: Thanks — I'm going to open a bug (ENG-1347) to either add a fallback shim in SDK when aiohttp<3.9 is present or to make dependency explicit. For now, quick mitigation for your CI: add a job step before install to `pip install --upgrade \"aiohttp>=3.9\"` (or update your constraints file). That should unblock you.

nate_dev: Installing aiohttp>=3.9 in CI fixed startup. App is back to normal. :white_check_mark: Thanks.

ana_support: Glad that worked. We'll follow up on the ticket. One more thing: if you can't upgrade aiohttp globally, we can recommend isolating the service into a separate virtualenv/container that allows the newer aiohttp to avoid monorepo-wide changes.

sam_engineer: Also adding a short note to the SDK release notes and a compatibility test against pinned older aiohttp versions. If we decide the SDK should remain compatible, we'll push a 0.14.3 patch that avoids calling the new shim.

deploy-bot: [deploy] ENG-1347 opened by sam_engineer — label: sdk/compat, priority: P2

nate_dev: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Will keep this thread updated if anything else pops up during the rollout to staging.
